text:
samir.support: Heads up — multiple customers pinged SRE about sharp p95/p99 increases on text-generation endpoints since the canary rollout at ~00:10 UTC. Tickets from Acme and Shoply are high-priority.

maria.eng: I see it on the dashboards too. p95 went from ~180ms -> ~420ms and p99 spiked to ~1.2s on /v1/generate.

alex.sre: Rolling alert: infra.p99_latency > 800ms for service=runtime-api in prod-us-west. Alert fired 00:25 UTC.

kai.eng-runtime: Canary promotion completed at 00:12 UTC — runtime v2.14.0 across canary pool. Change set included batching heuristic tweak + new kernel selector + driver bump to 535.12.

samir.support: Can we confirm whether the regression is canary-only or everywhere? Customers saying ~20% of requests slow.

alex.sre: Quick check — traffic split: 5% canary, 95% stable. But p95 for stable nodes also bumped a bit, maybe due to routing fallback.

maria.eng: Pulling traces now. Example trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d. Looks like long compute span on token-gen step, 900ms compute on canary node.

kai.eng-runtime: That suggests kernel selector may be choosing a suboptimal path for some sequence lengths. We changed threshold for FP16 fused matmul.

jordan.pm: Priority: Mitigate customer impact first, then full root cause. Agreed?

alex.sre: Agreed. Proposed mitigations: 1) pause canary promotion / rollback canary to v2.13.5; 2) route traffic away from nodes with new driver; 3) apply a temporary request-level throttle to long-seq requests.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollback runtime-canary -> v2.13.5 (initiated by @alex.sre) at 00:40 UTC.

maria.eng: While rollback runs, we should add a runtime-level config to disable the new batching heuristic: 

```
# runtime config override (temp)
batching.heuristic.enabled=false
kernel.selector.mode=legacy
```

kai.eng-runtime: I can push that override to canary pool in ~5m. That should avoid the kernel path change while rollback finishes.

samir.support: Also sending status to impacted customers: acknowledge, mitigation in progress, ETA ~30m. cc @jordan.pm

alex.sre: Investigating logs: correlated errors show elevated GC compactions on host gpu-17, and GPU utilization spiky. Snippet: 

```
2026-03-12T00:22:13Z runtime[pid=4123]: compute_span=912ms seq_len=1024 kernel=matmul_fused_v2
2026-03-12T00:22:13Z runtime[pid=4123]: cache_miss=true kv_hits=0
```

maria.eng: kv cache miss rate did increase after canary. Could be cache eviction policy change in v2.14.0. That would explain long tail for repeated requests.

kai.eng-runtime: We did change KV cache TTL logic to be more aggressive. I'm rolling that change out of canary now (reverting).

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0312-02 (p99 latency regression). Severity P2.

alex.sre: Repro plan if needed for validation: run wrk against canary node with token lengths 512/1024/2048 and measure p95/p99. Example command: 

```
wrk -t12 -c200 -d60s http://canary-01.runtime.internal/v1/generate -s ./scripts/long-seq.lua
```

samir.support: I spun up a small litmus test using the same prompt set as Acme; saw p99 ~1.1s against canary-01, stable nodes 220ms.

maria.eng: After config override and kernel revert, canary p99 dropped to ~240ms within two minutes on canary-02. So override looks effective.

kai.eng-runtime: Rollback complete on canary pool to v2.13.5 at 01:05 UTC per deploy logs. Will continue monitoring.

alex.sre: Re-checking metrics: global p95 back to ~190ms, p99 ~260ms. Looks like mitigated.

jordan.pm: Good. What's next for root cause? We should bisect the v2.14.0 changes to isolate the exact culprit. Candidates: batching heuristic, kernel selector, KV TTL, driver bump.

maria.eng: I'll run a binary bisect in staging: apply each change one-by-one to a staging canary and run wrk suite. Will log results to the incident.

kai.eng-runtime: For the kernel selector, I can add verbose selection logs to see why path chosen for seq=1024. Add flag: 

```
--kernel-log=selection_verbose
```

alex.sre: Also check node-level differences: GPU driver 535.12 vs 534.x — compare perf counters. If driver causes slower matmuls, that's critical.

samir.support: Action items so far: 
- alex.sre: lead rollback & incident comms (in progress)
- kai.eng-runtime: revert KV TTL + push batching override (done)
- maria.eng: bisect in staging and attach perf traces (in progress)
- samir.support: customer updates + ticket triage (in progress)

deploy-bot: Notification: rollback job completed successfully at 01:05:12 UTC.

maria.eng: Early bisect update: enabling only the kernel selector change reproduces p99 bump in staging. Both KV TTL and batching heuristic toggles alone didn't on their own.

kai.eng-runtime: Ok that's actionable. Kernel selector fallback path is picking matmul_fused_v2 for certain sequence shapes which is slower on Ampere in our benchmarking. Will revert selector logic and add a canary-only guard.

alex.sre: For short-term mitigations we should: 
- keep rollback on prod canary/stable where necessary
- add selector safety checks: compare predicted exec time, fallback to legacy if > threshold
- schedule a controlled rollout with perf gates

jordan.pm: I'll coordinate release windows with customer communications and update the SLA page if needed.

samir.support: Closing loop with customers: sent update 01:25 UTC — change rolled back, mitigation in place, monitoring ongoing.

maria.eng: We'll keep the incident open until a safe v2.14.x release with the selector fix is promoted and we verify p99 stable for 24h.

alex.sre: Postmortem owners? assign to kai + maria, include perf artifacts, trace samples, and rollout checklist.

kai.eng-runtime: Assigned. I'll also add an automated perf gate that rejects kernel selector changes that increase p99 by >5% in staging with our long-tail workload.

samir.support: Thanks everyone — great cross-team response. Will update INC-2026-0312-02 with final timeline and next steps once bisect completes. :thumbsup:
